Loan Default Dataset

loan_data.Rd

A dataset of 45,000 personal loan applications used to demonstrate the boundarylogic workflow on a credit-risk classification problem.

Format

A data frame with 45,000 rows and 14 variables:

person_age

Age of the applicant (numeric).

person_gender

Gender of the applicant: "female" or "male". Integer-encoded in the example script as 0 = female, 1 = male.

person_education

Highest education level attained: "High School", "Associate", "Bachelor", "Master", or "Doctorate". Integer-encoded as an ordinal 0–4.

person_income

Annual income in USD (numeric).

person_emp_exp

Years of employment experience (numeric).

person_home_ownership

Home ownership status: "MORTGAGE", "OTHER", "OWN", or "RENT". Integer-encoded as 0–3 in the example script.

loan_amnt

Loan amount applied for in USD (numeric).

loan_intent

Stated purpose of the loan: "DEBTCONSOLIDATION", "EDUCATION", "HOMEIMPROVEMENT", "MEDICAL", "PERSONAL", or "VENTURE". Integer-encoded as 0–5.

loan_int_rate

Interest rate of the loan as a percentage (numeric).

loan_percent_income

Loan amount as a fraction of annual income (numeric).

cb_person_cred_hist_length

Length of credit history in years (numeric).

credit_score

Applicant credit score (numeric).

previous_loan_defaults_on_file

Whether a prior default is on record: "No" or "Yes". Integer-encoded as 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

loan_status

Binary outcome: 1 = default, 0 = no default.

Source

https://github.com/TSMathi/loan_approval_analysis/tree/main

Details

Access the raw file via:


read.csv(system.file("extdata", "loan_data.csv", package = "boundarylogic"))

The raw file contains character columns for person_gender, person_education, person_home_ownership, loan_intent, and previous_loan_defaults_on_file. These must be integer-encoded before passing to bl_prepare_data(). The example script scripts/03_loan_status_Boundary_Logic.R shows the encoding step and an iterative three-phase workflow, including a domain filter that retains only applicants with a prior default on file.
